newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua legislative crisis suggests bleak future.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua legislative crisis suggests bleak future.

text.p: Nicaragua's National Assembly is locked in a bitter legislative battle that may be a sign of things to come for President-elect Arnoldo Aleman when he takes power on Jan. 10, politicians said on Friday.

At issue is a series of controversial laws passed by outgoing legislators allied to the left-wing Sandinistas. Aleman's right-wing Liberal Alliance has said these laws were designed to tie the hands of the next government.

The Liberals argue that the laws were illegal because the National Assembly had been declared closed by its Liberal-dominated board of directors before the vote. But the Sandinistas continued passing laws and divvying up political positions in sessions boycotted by the pro-Liberal faction.

The Supreme Court was expected to rule before Dec. 23 whether the National Assembly was open or closed. But whatever its conclusion, the crisis threatens to produce sparks in the next National Assembly, which takes office on Jan. 9.

"Nicaragua will have a National Assembly that will experience traumas and frequent crises between the powers. My prognosis is for a conflictive National Assembly," Congressman Carlos Gallo of the Sandinista Renovation Movement told Reuters.

If the Supreme Court approves the laws, one of which strips Aleman of his power to name the Central Bank president, Aleman has vowed to crush the move in the next Assembly. His Liberal Alliance has 42 seats in the 93-member Assembly, the Sandinistas have 36, and nine smaller parties share the remaining 15. Aleman needs 48 votes to pass laws.
Sandinista leaders have questioned Aleman's claim to have the support he needs to control the legislature and have accused him of wanting to dominate the National Assembly.

"Aleman wants to control the legislature and he thinks the legislature should be subordinated to the executive," former Sandinista President Daniel Ortega said. "But this is not the case and this is why we are working to provide a board of directors for the next National Assembly that is independent of the executive."
